issues.description: import-notation 'url' branch inverts the filter polarity and short-circuits the validity check
issues.detail: When primary is 'url', the guard returns early if params contain 'url(' — skipping the inner check entirely. Sibling rules gate on the opposite token. Either this is a semantic bug allowing mixed/malformed cases to pass unvalidated, or it is correct but undocumented. Verify semantics and add a one-line spec comment on the inverted polarity.

issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex lacks the /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it, breaking case-insensitive contract symmetry
issues.detail: CSS treats keyframe selector tokens like from/to case-insensitively. HAS_KEYWORD uses /i; HAS_PERCENTAGE does not. The asymmetry strengthens one branch's precondition and risks dropping legitimate rules like `FROM { ... }` when primary is 'keyword'. Apply the case flag uniformly or document why it differs.

issues.description: selectorRegex /./ sentinel leaks 'no filter' as a regex that matches everything
issues.detail: Using /./ to mean 'walk everything' complects filter-or-no-filter with a regex value. walkRules already accepts an absent filter; branch on whether a filter exists and call walkRules(cb) vs walkRules(regex, cb). Cleaner contract, smaller surface, intent visible at the call site.

issues.description: Repeated fast-path regex pattern across rules has no shared abstraction or documented over-approximation contract
issues.detail: Six rules now reinvent the same idiom: compile a presence regex, bail early if absent. The implicit contract — 'fast-path must over-approximate the slow-path' — is unspecified. Lift the option-to-regex mapping into a small table or helper, and document the over-approximation invariant so future contributors don't accidentally tighten a filter into a false negative.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes duplicate parser-side keyword sets and may drift without a documented link
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_KEYWORD and friends encode subsets of what valueParser/parseSelector later proves. The constants derive from the same source sets — the right call — but the dependency is implicit. Add a brief comment naming the invariant so future edits to keyword sets update both sides together.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED guard in font-weight-notation misreads mixed values containing both keywords and numbers
issues.detail: When primary is 'numeric', the guard short-circuits if no named keyword is present, but a value like '400 bold' contains both. The predicate conflates 'value contains a named keyword' with 'value is named'. Make the fast-path answer the right question: 'does this value contain anything that needs conversion?'

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is a sound, well-shaped performance optimization: cheap presence regexes gate expensive parser passes across six rules. Two concrete concerns warrant fixing before merge: the import-notation 'url' branch inverts filter polarity and may skip the very case it should validate, and the keyframe-selector HAS_PERCENTAGE/HAS_KEYWORD pair has an inconsistent case-insensitive flag. The emerging fast-reject pattern needs a named abstraction and a documented over-approximation contract; the /./ sentinel and inline duplication of parser keyword data are minor cleanups. Verify the two suspect lines, then ship.
